- If sentiment shows strong bullish (e.g., +1.00) in recent days, model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment shows strong bearish (e.g., -1.00), model often under-forecasts; adjust downward bias or add early correction factor.
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” decay to subsequent forecasts.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (e.g., 0.00 or 0.25), model often fails to capture mean reversion; add a 3–5 day moving average correction.
- If true outcome shows strong divergence from forecast in first 5–7 days, model is lagging; adjust horizon to include early correction (e.g., shift forecast down 1–2 days if sentiment is bearish).
- Model consistently overestimates 30-day mean in bullish sentiment periods; apply a 10–15% downward bias to long-term forecasts when sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment turns negative after a peak, model often fails to reverse; add a “sentiment reversal” trigger to reduce forecast slope after day 10–14.
